Package com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.infrastructure.security

Class InMemoryJwtDenylistAdapter

java.lang.Object
com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.infrastructure.security.InMemoryJwtDenylistAdapter
All Implemented Interfaces:
JwtDenylist
@Component public class InMemoryJwtDenylistAdapter extends Object implements JwtDenylist
In-process implementation of JwtDenylist (design §8.3).

Single-node v1 (TBD-1 covers a Redis-backed multi-node variant). Backed by a ConcurrentHashMap so reads and writes from the JWT filter are lock-free.

Eviction strategy is two-pronged:

  • Read-time: contains(UUID) drops an expired entry it observes, keeping the map bounded between sweeps under steady load.
  • Scheduled: sweep() runs every 60 s as a backstop, draining entries whose owning request never came back to discover them.

Sensitive-data discipline: the jti appears in log output only at DEBUG level (REQ-SEC-004).

    • add

      public void add(UUID jti, OffsetDateTime expiresAt)
      Description copied from interface: JwtDenylist
      Records that the JWT identified by jti is logged out until at least expiresAt. Calls with an already-past expiresAt are a no-op (no point keeping an entry the next read would drop anyway).
      Specified by:
      add in interface JwtDenylist

    • contains

      public boolean contains(UUID jti)
      Description copied from interface: JwtDenylist
      Returns true iff jti is on the denylist and its recorded expiry is still in the future. Implementations SHOULD evict an expired entry observed during this call (read-time eviction) so the denylist stays bounded between scheduled sweeps.
      Specified by:
      contains in interface JwtDenylist

    • sweep

      @Scheduled(fixedDelay=60000L) public void sweep()
      Drops every entry whose recorded expiry is in the past. Runs every 60 seconds in a Spring-managed scheduler thread (REQ-AUTH-011: the denylist remains bounded by the configured JWT lifetime).
